clue.text: Hand in middle of puppet, possibly? Show two little boys

parts.note: the two central letters of puppet are both P, which could be described as a double P
to air something is to show it in public
Roy and Al, two boys' names in short form

explanation.surface: A puppeteer's hand inside a puppet puts on a show starring two small boys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly?' flags the playful description: the middle of PUPPET is PP, a double P. In cribbage, a double pair royal is four cards of the same rank.
explanation.definitionFit: In cribbage scoring, four of a kind held together is a named combination of cards, i.e. a hand.

clue.text: Within lateral partition, hairlike structures, indefinite number opening

indicators.note: the hair-like structures and the number sit within the words for a partition at the side

parts.note: a side fence is a partition at the side
cilia are tiny hair-like structures on cells
N stands for an unspecified number in maths

explanation.surface: A biology description of hair-like cells packed inside a membrane, with a number of them opening up.
explanation.walkthrough: CILIAN goes after the first two letters of SIDE FENCE. The Sicilian Defence is a chess opening.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian Defence is a standard sequence of first chess moves, a classic named opening.

clue.text: The sad criminal with muscle in band of assassins

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of the sad are bent out of shape

parts.note: quad is short for quadriceps, the thigh muscle

explanation.surface: Sad, criminal muscle men join a gang of killers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges THE SAD into DEATHS; 'with' just joins on QUAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A death squad is an armed group sent out to kill people, a gang of hired killers.

clue.text: Insults thrown after end of four months on a British Overseas Territory

indicators.note: after places the thrown insults behind the shared ending of the months

parts.note: September, October, November and December all end in BER
slung insults are mud, as in mudslinging

explanation.surface: Abuse is hurled at a British colony after the final months of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermuda is an island group in the Atlantic that remains a British Overseas Territory.

clue.text: Earth healing heart?

definitions.meaning: a kind of earth or soil
the heart of the word healing is ALI

explanation.surface: Is soil a remedy for the heart?
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a riddle: the middle letters of 'healing' are ALI, the boxer whose birth name was Cassius Clay.
explanation.definitionFit: Clay is a heavy, sticky type of soil, so it is a kind of earth.

clue.text: A doctor unfortunately can heal and cures lawyer after an accident?

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: unfortunately signals the letters of can heal and cures go awry

explanation.surface: A doctor regrets that healing and cures are spoiled by litigious lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns CAN HEAL and CURES into ULANCECHASER; 'and' is part of the link, not fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambulance chaser is a lawyer who seeks clients among the injured, a disparaging term for personal-injury touting.

clue.text: Member welcomed by literati once shifting between Yale and Harvard, say?

indicators.note: welcomed by means the member is taken inside the shifted letters
shifting tells us the letters of literati once move about

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A member of a club welcomed by the intellectual elite as he moves between two Ivy League universities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges the fodder to give INTERCOLIATE, which 'welcomed by' opens to take in the member. Yale and Harvard are colleges, so a match between them is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercollegiate means taking place between colleges, such as a contest between two universities.

clue.text: Italian broadcast in stereo

indicators.note: broadcast, meaning scattered, suggests the letters of in stereo are spread around

explanation.surface: An Italian programme aired in stereo sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges IN STEREO.
explanation.definitionFit: Torinese describes a person from Turin, Torino in Italian, so it is a type of Italian.

clue.text: Sharp needle — no need for it, day surgery's ending

indicators.note: no need means the letters of the word need are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
Mon is the usual abbreviation for Monday

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sharp needle is unnecessary for day surgery, which is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no need' strips NEED from NEEDLE, leaving LE; 'for it' is link. 'ending' gives Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemony taste is tart and acidic, so sharp in flavour.

clue.text: Player is inspired by Milton (abridged)

indicators.note: inspired, breathed in, means is is taken inside the cut-down name
abridged means the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Milton Obote was a president of Uganda

explanation.surface: A performer is inspired by a shortened Milton, the poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Milton' looks like the poet but is Milton Obote, Uganda's former leader; OBOTE less E is OBOT, with IS taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist is a musician who plays the oboe, so a player in an orchestra.

clue.text: Beauty in unelected British leaders?

definitions.meaning: a girl chosen as the beauty of a spring festival
Theresa May took over as Prime Minister without a general election, and the monarch is never elected

explanation.surface: Beauty among British rulers that nobody voted for.
explanation.walkthrough: When this ran, Theresa May had just become Prime Minister without a general election; the monarch, then the Queen, is never elected.
explanation.definitionFit: The May Queen is a girl crowned at English May Day celebrations, chosen for her looks.

clue.text: House backing newspaper, though not leader

indicators.note: backing means the remaining letters are read in reverse
not leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A house backs a newspaper, though not its editor.
explanation.walkthrough: TIMES without its first letter is IMES; 'backing' turns it round. A semi is a semi-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi is British shorthand for a semi-detached house, one of a joined pair.

clue.text: Fancy dealings with church look anything but straightforward?

indicators.note: fancy, meaning elaborate, suggests the letters of dealings are dressed up anew

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Fancy dealings with the church look suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges DEALINGS into SIDEGLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A side-glance is a sideways look, literally not straight ahead.

clue.text: Cog so pricy to fix, spinning as a ship's navigational aid, say?

definitions.text: spinning as a ship's navigational aid, say?

indicators.note: fixing something means rearranging its parts, so the letters of cog so pricy are reworked

explanation.surface: A spinning cog in a ship's navigation instrument is so expensive to repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fix' rearranges COG SO PRICY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gyroscopic describes a spinning wheel that holds its orientation, as in a ship's gyrocompass.

clue.text: Agonising facts cut into me

indicators.note: into means the shortened facts are placed inside the setter's name

parts.note: me is the setter, whose pseudonym is Paul

indicators.note: cut means the last letter is chopped off

parts.note: info is short for information, facts

explanation.surface: Painful facts cut deep into me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' is the setter speaking, whose pseudonym is Paul; 'cut' drops the last letter of the facts word, giving INF, and 'into' places that inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agonising causes great suffering, i.e. it hurts badly.

clue.text: Difficult taking wrench into work

indicators.note: into means the wrench goes inside the word for work

parts.note: to ply is to work at a trade
to rick a joint is to wrench or sprain it

explanation.surface: A tricky job using a wrench at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prickly person or problem is touchy and hard to handle, so difficult.

clue.text: Elderly, compatible to some extent

definitions.meaning: people who get along fairly well are, in a small way, rubbing along together

explanation.surface: Older people are getting along fairly well.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting on a bit is an informal idiom for growing old, and literally means liking each other slightly.

clue.text: Why Saturday never comes alone?

parts.note: if Friday has no end, Saturday can never arrive; and a person without companions is alone

explanation.surface: A riddle about why a weekend never arrives for someone on their own.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as FRI END LESS: Friday has no end, so Saturday never comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Without friends means lonely, alone in the world.

clue.text: Team gloated

definitions.meaning: a group working together, as on a ship
an old past tense of crow, to gloat

explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a working group of people, as on a boat or film set.

clue.text: Pretty me in female bowler, say?

indicators.note: in means me goes inside the female animal

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a bowler is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: Calling me pretty in a lady's bowler hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective but is the adverb: pretty good means somewhat good.
explanation.definitionFit: As adverbs, pretty and somewhat both mean to a moderate degree, fairly.

clue.text: Female animal is back

explanation.surface: A female creature has returned.
explanation.definitionFit: A hind is a female red deer; hind also means rear, as in hind legs.

clue.text: See 17
Bird entrails, but not of rook

indicators.note: but not tells us to remove the letters of the word of

parts.note: offal is the edible innards of an animal
taken as written
to rook someone is to swindle or con them

explanation.surface: A bird's innards, though not those of the rook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rook' looks like another bird but means swindle, CON. OFFAL minus OF leaves FAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon is a bird of prey, a fast-flying hunting raptor.

clue.text: Piece of meat stuffing baguettes, I once recalled

indicators.note: recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
stuffing says the letters are packed inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Remembering meat stuffed into baguettes long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Piece of meat stuffing' as the definition, but 'stuffing' is the hidden-word signal: the answer is stuffed inside 'baguettes, I once', read backwards ('recalled').
explanation.definitionFit: A noisette is a small round boneless cut of lamb, a piece of meat.
